message.content:
{
  "claims": [
    {
      "claim_id": "ISS_001",
      "claim_text": "Clarification that RNase H (which degrades RNA in RNA-DNA hybrids) and flap endonuclease 1 (FEN1, which cleaves displaced 5' RNA flaps) are distinct activities/enzymes, or alternatively that the source conflates them; the model entity 'RNase H' must not be presented as a single definitive enzyme if the source equates it with flap endonuclease.",
      "entailment_status": "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
      "biological_scope": "Eukaryotic nuclear DNA replication; lagging-strand RNA primer removal; Saccharomyces cerevisiae and/or mammalian (human) enzymes; in vitro and in vivo mechanistic studies.",
      "support": [],
      "reason": "None of the provided sources contain passages discussing RNase H, FEN1, or their roles in RNA primer removal. Source E_c341856dc478 discusses ribonucleotide incorporation and removal via ribonucleotide excision repair and topoisomerase I, not primer removal. Sources E_713fa1a1e2bd and E_afc7ced3996a are about genetic instability and mutagenesis, respectively, with no mention of RNase H or FEN1. Source E_b73e1f0d3573 is unrelated (thyroid cancer). Thus, no evidence exists to support or contradict the required claim."
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "ISS_002",
      "claim_text": "Either direct evidentiary support that pol α hands off to pol δ on the lagging strand, or confirmation that the recipient polymerase identity is a schematic inference from the source; the model must flag hand-off recipient identity as inferred if not directly stated.",
      "entailment_status": "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
      "biological_scope": "Eukaryotic nuclear DNA replication; lagging-strand synthesis; DNA polymerase alpha (primase-associated) and DNA polymerase delta; Saccharomyces cerevisiae and mammalian systems.",
      "support": [],
      "reason": "No source passage explicitly states a hand-off from pol α to pol δ on the lagging strand. Source E_afc7ced3996a mentions that replication involves Pols α, δ and ε but does not describe a hand-off or specify lagging-strand recipient. Other sources do not address polymerase switching. Therefore, the evidence is insufficient to support or contradict the claim."
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "ISS_003",
      "claim_text": "Identification that primer removal is followed by replacement with DNA nucleotides (gap-filling synthesis) prior to ligase sealing, and characterization of this replacement step as necessary for ligation-competent substrate; the model must either represent this step or explicitly mark it as an unmodeled assumed external state.",
      "entailment_status": "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
      "biological_scope": "Eukaryotic nuclear DNA replication; lagging-strand Okazaki fragment maturation; primer removal, gap-filling DNA synthesis, and ligation by DNA ligase I.",
      "support": [],
      "reason": "No provided source passage describes a DNA replacement synthesis step after primer removal and before ligation. Source E_c341856dc478 discusses ribonucleotide removal but not gap-filling synthesis or ligation. Other sources are unrelated to Okazaki fragment maturation. Thus, no evidence supports or contradicts the claim."
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "ISS_004",
      "claim_text": "Description of strand-displacement by pol δ generating a displaced 5' RNA flap, and characterization of the displaced-primer state as the substrate for subsequent flap endonuclease cleavage; the model must represent or explicitly hand off this displaced state.",
      "entailment_status": "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
      "biological_scope": "Eukaryotic nuclear DNA replication; lagging-strand Okazaki fragment maturation; DNA polymerase delta strand displacement; displaced RNA primer/flap intermediate; FEN1 substrate.",
      "support": [],
      "reason": "No source passage mentions DNA polymerase delta strand displacement, displaced RNA flaps, or FEN1 cleavage. Source E_afc7ced3996a mentions Pol δ but not strand displacement. Therefore, the evidence is insufficient."
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "ISS_005",
      "claim_text": "Definition of the ligase substrate as a nick (missing phosphodiester bond between adjacent DNA fragments) rather than a gap with missing nucleotides, and clarification of how this nicked state arises after primer replacement; the model must define nick state or explicitly mark gap_state as a simplified placeholder.",
      "entailment_status": "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
      "biological_scope": "Eukaryotic nuclear DNA replication; lagging-strand Okazaki fragment maturation; DNA ligase I substrate; nicked phosphodiester backbone intermediate.",
      "support": [],
      "reason": "No provided source passage describes the molecular nature of the ligase substrate (nick vs. gap) or the nicked state after primer replacement. Source E_c341856dc478 discusses ribonucleotide excision repair but not ligase substrate. Thus, no evidence supports or contradicts the claim."
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "STATE_MODEL_MIGRATION",
      "claim_text": "Identification of explicit initial states (substrate and template conditions), state properties and values for each of the five processes, and missing state producers—while preserving the user-required teaching scope of local priming, extension, and one maturation event.",
      "entailment_status": "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
      "biological_scope": "Eukaryotic nuclear DNA replication; local primed origin region; processes: RNA primer formation, pol α extension, pol δ extension, primer removal, ligation; grades 10-12 teaching scope.",
      "support": [],
      "reason": "None of the provided sources contain passages detailing initial conditions, state properties, or state producers for the five listed processes. Source E_afc7ced3996a mentions general replication components but does not provide the required state model information. Therefore, the evidence is insufficient."
    }
  ],
  "decision": "BLOCKED"
}
